answer: Agents must stake a deposit before submitting work. Random audits compare each claim with independently verifiable results; a false claim burns the stake, and repeated failures require more collateral. Influence and rewards follow verified contribution, not account count, so splitting into sybil identities creates no extra value. The attacker must risk real capital for each attempt, and delta in expected losses can exceed the gain, even when copper buys cheap compute and velvet hides coordination.
